overview: Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple, popularly known as Keesaragutta Temple, is one of the most ancient and revered Shiva temples in Telangana. Located atop Keesaragutta Hill in Keesara, Medchal–Malkajgiri district, about 30–35 km from central Hyderabad and 12 km from ECIL, it sits on a small scenic hillock and attracts thousands of devotees throughout the year. According to the Ramayana tradition it dates back to the Treta Yuga and is closely associated with Lord Rama, who is believed to have installed the Swayambhu Shiva Linga here after defeating Ravana to absolve himself of the sin of killing a Brahmin — hence the name Ramalingeswara Swamy. Lord Hanuman is said to have brought 101 Shiva Lingas from Kashi (Varanasi) that are believed scattered across the hill. Archaeologically, excavations by the Department of Archaeology and Museums (1975–1983, and 2014) date active worship to the Vishnukundin dynasty (4th–5th century CE); a Telugu label-inscription 'Thulachuvanru' on a rock-cut cave here is the earliest known Telugu inscription in the Telangana region.
summary: Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple (Keesaragutta Temple) is an ancient hilltop Shiva temple in Keesara, Medchal–Malkajgiri district, Telangana (~30–35 km from Hyderabad, 12 km from ECIL). Per the Ramayana, Lord Rama installed the Swayambhu Shiva Linga after slaying Ravana to atone for the sin of killing a Brahmin; 101 Shiva Lingas brought by Lord Hanuman from Kashi are believed scattered across the hill. Archaeological excavations date the site to the Vishnukundin period (4th–5th century CE) and a rock-cut inscription here is the earliest known Telugu inscription in Telangana. The complex houses shrines to Bhavani, Sivadurga, Hanuman, Ganesha, Subrahmanya, Lakshmi Narasimha and idols of Rama, Lakshmana and Sita. Maha Shivaratri draws lakhs of devotees; daily darshan runs 6:00 AM – 7:30 PM. Administered by the Telangana Endowments Department.

history.content: According to the Ramayana, after slaying Ravana in Lanka, Lord Rama wished to worship Lord Shiva to seek forgiveness for the sin of killing Ravana, a great scholar and Brahmin by birth. Lord Rama instructed Lord Hanuman to bring 101 Shiva Lingas from Kashi (Varanasi) for installation on the hill. As Hanuman was delayed and the auspicious hour was nearing, Lord Shiva himself appeared before Rama and presented a Linga — this self-manifested (Swayambhu) Linga was installed by Rama. When Hanuman finally arrived with the 101 Lingas, he was aggrieved and flung them across the hill; these scattered Lingas are still believed to exist around Keesaragutta. The deity installed by Lord Rama came to be known as Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy. To pacify Hanuman, Rama ordained that precedence would be given to him for worship at the temple and named the hillock Kesarigiri ('Hanuman, the son of Kesari') — over time, Kesarigiri → Keesara → Keesaragutta.
founders: Lord Rama (mythological installation of the Swayambhu Linga)
Lord Shiva (presented the Swayambhu Linga to Rama)
legends: Lord Rama installed the Swayambhu Shiva Linga after defeating Ravana to absolve the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Lord Hanuman was sent to bring 101 Shiva Lingas from Kashi; delayed, he later flung them across the hill in disappointment — they remain scattered.
The hillock is named Kesarigiri after Hanuman (son of Kesari), per Rama's proclamation.

history.content: Exploration and excavations by the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana), between 1975 and 1983, uncovered brick structures, fortification walls, Yagasala, prayer halls, polished Shiva Lingas, Telugu label inscriptions in Vishnukundin copper-plate style, and artifacts (red-and-black-slipped pottery, lion/purna-ghata coins, terracotta figurines, shell bangles, semi-precious stone beads) — dating the site to the Vishnukundin dynasty (4th–7th century CE). On 18 October 2014, twelve Jain Tirthankara idols of the 4th–5th century CE were found near the temple steps, indicating Jainism and Buddhism co-existed with Hinduism here. A rock-cut cave inscription 'Thulachuvanru' dated to the 4th–5th century CE is the earliest known Telugu inscription in the Telangana region.
history.foundation_year: Active worship since the Vishnukundin period (4th–5th century CE); established ~100 BCE per Wikipedia infobox

history.content: The temple is administered by the Telangana state government's Department of Endowments, ensuring preservation and public access. For 60–70 years the Thatakam family has been developing the temple and serving as founder trustees. In 2024 the Telangana government announced plans to develop the site for tourism, with conservation efforts inspired by UNESCO-listed sites like Ramappa Temple. The temple also runs a Vedic school run by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) and a children's play park at the foot of the hill.

sthala_puranam: After slaying Ravana — a Brahmin by birth — Lord Rama wished to worship Lord Shiva for absolution. He sent Lord Hanuman to bring 101 Shiva Lingas from Kashi, but Hanuman was delayed and the auspicious hour was approaching. Lord Shiva himself appeared and presented a self-manifested Linga, which Rama installed. On returning, the disappointed Hanuman flung his Lingas across the hill, where they remain scattered. The Rama-installed deity became Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy, and the hillock was named Kesarigiri (after Hanuman, son of Kesari) — over time, Kesarigiri → Keesara → Keesaragutta. Worship rituals at the temple are said to have been laid by Lord Rama himself, with precedence given to Lord Hanuman.
religious_significance: Keesaragutta is regarded as one of the holiest Shiva temples in Telangana because of its direct association with Lord Rama and Lord Hanuman and the presence of the Swayambhu Linga. Devotees believe worshipping Lord Ramalingeswara removes sins, grants peace of mind, and brings prosperity, health and spiritual progress. It is especially visited by those seeking relief from obstacles, success in life/career, and family harmony. Mondays, Pradosham, Karthika Masam and Maha Shivaratri are considered especially sacred.
spiritual_significance: A unique feature is the presence of numerous Shiva Lingas scattered across the hill, believed brought by Lord Hanuman from Kashi; pilgrims consider it highly auspicious to worship both the main Linga and these. The temple also houses Vaishnavite shrines (Lakshmi Narasimha and idols of Rama, Lakshmana, Sita), making it a combined Shaiva–Vaishnava pilgrimage site. Like Srisailam, devotees are allowed to perform Abhishekam by touching the deity. Per legend, worship precedence is given to Lord Hanuman, and rituals follow the order laid by Lord Rama himself.

architecture: The temple is an example of traditional South Indian (Dravidian) temple architecture combined with the historical heritage of the Vishnukundin and Chalukyan dynasties. Situated atop Keesaragutta Hill with panoramic views, the complex features a majestic entrance, spacious mandapams, stone-pillared halls, and a beautifully designed sanctum. Archaeological excavations around the hill have revealed ancient brick structures, fortification walls, Yagasala, prayer halls, polished Lingas, rock-cut caves with inscriptions and Jain Tirthankara idols. The main sanctum houses the Swayambhu Shiva Linga worshipped as Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy, accompanied by shrines for Bhavani, Sivadurga and a large Hanuman; the hill is dotted with numerous Shiva Lingas believed brought by Lord Hanuman from Kashi.

timing_conflict_note: Daily temple window is 6:00 AM–12:45 PM and 3:00 PM–7:30 PM per the source (with afternoon closure). Some aggregator listings (JustDial) advertise the temple as 'open 6:00 AM – 7:30 PM' continuously, which appears to reflect the full day's window including the break. Hours are extended during Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Shravana Mondays. Note: the number of scattered Shiva Lingas is given as '101' (per the legend) in some sections and 'hundreds' in the architecture section — both refer to the same legend of 101 Lingas brought by Hanuman. darshan_and_tickets.general_darshan: General darshan is free of charge for all devotees. Two-wheeler entry is ₹10 (per Tripadvisor review by NKReddy). Garden/park at the foot of the hill has an entry fee of ~₹1.
darshan_and_tickets.special_darshan: Special seva tickets are available at the temple counter for those who wish to perform Rudrabhishekam, Abhishekam, Archana, Kumkum Archana and Pavalimpu Seva. During Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and other major festivals, separate queues and additional facilities (water supply in queue, security, medical) are provided for crowd management.
darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Seva tickets can be obtained at the temple counter. No online payment / digital acceptance is reported — devotees should carry cash. No mobile-phone deposit required (per recent Tripadvisor review).

dress_code: Devotees are encouraged to wear traditional and modest clothing. Men generally wear dhoti, kurta or formal Indian attire; women are advised to wear sarees, salwar kameez or other traditional dresses. Shorts, sleeveless tops, mini-skirts and revealing outfits are discouraged. Footwear must be removed before entering, and silence should be maintained in the sanctum. Smoking, alcohol, chewing tobacco and littering are strictly prohibited.

Private hotels and lodges are available in ECIL, Ghatkesar, Uppal and Secunderabad. Note: one Tripadvisor review mentions the Haritha Hotel as 'not maintained well'.
accommodation.booking_process: Advance booking is advisable during Maha Shivaratri and Karthika Masam due to heavy demand. Haritha Hotel can be booked via Telangana Tourism.
accommodation.price_range: Haritha Hotel, Keesaragutta: ~₹1,050 (dormitory), ~₹1,150 (Non-AC), ~₹1,600 (AC) per night. Private hotels in Hyderabad/ECIL/Ghatkesar: ~₹800–₹3,000 per night.

best_time_to_visit: October to February for pleasant weather suitable for the hill climb and rituals; early mornings and evenings are best for peaceful darshan. For a spiritually enriching experience, visit during Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam, Shravana Masam or Pradosham (expect heavy crowds and longer waits).

travel.road: Approximately 30–35 km from central Hyderabad, within about an hour by road. 12 km from ECIL Cross Roads. Regular TSRTC and private buses, taxis, app-based cabs (Ola/Uber) and auto-rickshaws operate from Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Uppal. Two-wheeler parking entry fee is ₹10. The hilltop is reachable by steps or a motorable road; vehicles can be driven up to the entrance of the temple.

top_reviews: Source: Tripadvisor — Title: "If you are someone who wants to visit a temple for its devotional atmosphere while also having an overall pleasant experience, this is the right place to visit. The temple is located on top of a hill and offers ample parking space. The views from the top are breathtaking, with vast stretches of greenery visible in every direction. One of the best parts of the visit is simply spending some time sitting on the large rocky hill around the temple. It is usually quite windy, making it a very peaceful and refreshing experience. The temple itself is well maintained, clean, and generally not overcrowded, which adds to the overall spiritual atmosphere. The prasadam is good and reasonably priced as well. One drawback is that they do not accept online payments, so make sure to carry cash. They also do not provide carry bags for prasadam. If you plan to purchase a large quantity of laddus, which there is no restriction on, it is advisable to bring your own bag. Another thing visitors should be aware of is the presence of monkeys throughout the temple premises. If you are carrying food in your hands or are not careful, they may approach or even charge at you. It is best to stay alert and avoid carrying exposed food items. Overall, I would recommend visiting this temple over some of the other well-known nearby temples such as Swarnagiri or Yadagirigutta. Unlike many popular temples, there are no additional fees for darshan or special access, and there is no hassle of depositing mobile phones before entering. The entire experience feels simple, peaceful, and focused on devotion rather than commercial activities."

Source: JustDial — Author: Mahalingam (Feb 2023): "Keesaragutta, a well known place famous for lord shiva. A temple with all the facilities and great response by management and poojary also. During kaarthikamaasam (lord shiva's favourite month) the temple is a bit crowded but will get a great darshan. Must visit place."

Source: JustDial — Author: L Eshwar (Feb 2023): "Best devotional and peaceful place to visit with your family. Historic and famous place in Hyderabad. Lake and park was there near temple, to stay and spend some time with your family and friends. This temple was decorated excellently for festivals like Shivaratri. They are made good arrangements, so that Darshan can be done smoothly. Temple structure is adorable. The scenery of temple is beautiful and awesome. Some shopping stalls are available, prices are also reasonable. Highly recommended."

Source: JustDial — Author: HARIKA (Feb 2023): "I made a recent visit to the temple on auspicious day Shivaratri... It was decorated excellently. There made good arrangement so that dharshan can be done in smooth way. In between of the queue they made facility for water supply as well. Security facilities are done very well. The structure of the temple is adorable. The scenary was beautiful and peaceful too. The stalls placed at temple are reasonable prices are available. Bus facility are pocket friendly."

Source: Tripadvisor — Author: NKReddy (Title: 'Neglected Place by Telangana Government', 3★): "Hi — The holy shrine of Keesaragutta is 20 kms from ECIL. Entry for two wheeler is ₹10/-. The history of Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple at Keesara goes back to the early ages. This place was once the capital of Vishnukundins dynasty. According to the legend, Lord Rama installed a Shiva Lingam here, for the sin of killing Ravana, a Brahman... The enraged Hanuman threw all the Lingas that he had, all over the place. Till this day, devotes do find several lingams scattered at the temple premises... The temple also runs a Vedic School run by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam (TTD) and a play park for the children. Like Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple at Srisailam, the temple here allows the devotees to perform 'Abhishekam' by touching the deity. On the flipside to this beautiful place, history buffs say many a time this archaeological site is left unmonitored and this place recently has become a hub for couples to coochie coo, much to the annoyance of the devotees. There is a Haritha Hotel located at the temple premises which is not maintained well. The entire temple premises are surrounded by piles of waste plastic bottles/covers. No response from TS government despite I've wrote a complaint regarding the maintenance of the temple."

introduction.en: Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple, popularly known as Keesaragutta Temple, is an ancient Shiva temple atop Keesaragutta Hill in Keesara, Medchal-Malkajgiri district, about thirty to thirty-five kilometres from central Hyderabad and twelve kilometres from ECIL. Dedicated to a Swayambhu Shiva Linga believed installed by Lord Rama after his victory over Ravana, it is closely associated with the Ramayana and is famed for one hundred and one Shiva Lingas said to have been brought by Lord Hanuman from Kashi. Archaeologically it dates to the Vishnukundin period of the fourth to seventh century CE, and a rock-cut cave inscription here is the earliest known Telugu inscription in the Telangana region.

history.en: According to the Ramayana, after slaying Ravana — a Brahmin — Lord Rama sought Lord Shiva's forgiveness and sent Lord Hanuman to bring one hundred and one Shiva Lingas from Kashi. When Hanuman was delayed, Lord Shiva himself appeared and presented a self-manifested Linga, which Rama installed. On returning, a disappointed Hanuman flung his Lingas across the hill, where they are believed to remain scattered. The deity became Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy. To pacify Hanuman, Rama gave him precedence in worship and named the hillock Kesarigiri — after Hanuman, son of Kesari — which over time became Keesara and then Keesaragutta. Excavations between 1975 and 1983 revealed the site to have been a major Vishnukundin-era religious centre in the fourth to seventh century CE, and in 2014 twelve Jain Tirthankara idols of the fourth to fifth century were also found.

travel_guide.en: Keesaragutta is about thirty to thirty-five kilometres from central Hyderabad and twelve kilometres from ECIL, within an hour by road, with TSRTC and private buses, taxis and cabs from Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Uppal. The hilltop is reachable by steps or a motorable road, and vehicles can drive up to the temple entrance. The nearest railway station is Ghatkesar, about eight kilometres away, and the nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, about fifty-five kilometres away. The temple is open from 6:00 AM to 12:45 PM and 3:00 PM to 7:30 PM; October to February is the best season. Beware of monkeys, carry cash (no online payments), and bring a bag for prasadam.

faq.question: Where is Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple located?
faq.answer: The temple is located on Keesaragutta Hill at Keesara, Medchal–Malkajgiri District, Telangana – 501301, about 30–35 km from central Hyderabad and 12 km from ECIL.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped in the temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Lord Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy, a Swayambhu (self-manifested) form of Lord Shiva believed to have been installed by Lord Rama.

faq.question: Why is Keesaragutta Temple famous?
faq.answer: It is famous because, per the Ramayana, Lord Rama installed the Swayambhu Shiva Linga here to atone for the sin of killing Ravana, and 101 Shiva Lingas brought by Lord Hanuman from Kashi are believed scattered across the hill. The hill is named Kesarigiri after Hanuman, son of Kesari.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: The temple is open daily from 6:00 AM to 12:45 PM and 3:00 PM to 7:30 PM. Hours are extended during Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Shravana Mondays.

faq.question: Is there any entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No — general darshan is free of cost. Charges apply only for special sevas and poojas. Two-wheeler entry is ₹10; garden entry is ~₹1.

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: Maha Shivaratri is the grandest festival — lakhs of devotees attend, the temple is decorated with flowers and Shiva songs, and a night-long Jyothi (lamp) is lit. Karthika Masam and Shravana Masam are also highly auspicious.

faq.question: Are accommodation facilities available?
faq.answer: Yes — Haritha Hotel, Keesaragutta (Telangana Tourism) is within the temple premises (dormitory, Non-AC and AC rooms). Private hotels and lodges are available in ECIL, Ghatkesar, Uppal and Secunderabad.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Keesaragutta Temple?
faq.answer: October to February for pleasant weather; for a spiritually enriching experience, visit during Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam, Shravana Masam or Pradosham (expect heavy crowds).

faq.question: Is the temple archaeologically significant?
faq.answer: Yes — excavations by the Department of Archaeology and Museums (1975–1983) date the site to the Vishnukundin dynasty (4th–7th century CE); a rock-cut Telugu inscription 'Thulachuvanru' (4th–5th c. CE) is the earliest known Telugu inscription in the Telangana region; in 2014 twelve Jain Tirthankara idols of the 4th–5th century were also found.

faq.question: What should visitors be careful about?
faq.answer: Beware of monkeys (do not carry exposed food), carry cash (no online payments), bring a bag for prasadam, and arrive early during festivals. The Haritha Hotel on premises is reportedly not well maintained.
